title: Police apology sought for `senseless' death
subtitle: The family of an 18-year-old man shot and killed by police in Riverdale Park last week wants an apology for his "senseless" death.
article: The family of an 18-year-old man shot and killed by police in Riverdale Park last week wants an apology for his "senseless" death.
Muna Bafagih, 58, the mother of Alwy Al Nadhir, who died in hospital after being gunned down Halloween night, said yesterday she has it in her heart to forgive the officer who killed her only son.
"I am a good woman," she said. "I have faith in my religion. If it is written for him to die this way, okay. If they had come to apologize and say it's a mistake, I would have forgiven them."

Surrounded by her husband, three daughters, family and friends, Bafagih, frail and too stunned to cry, reclined on a couch in the basement of the family's apartment in a housing complex near Dundas St. W. and Spadina Ave.
Describing her son as an "innocent" victim of this tragedy, she's trying to understand why police would take such drastic action with someone like Al Nadhir.

A student at Central Technical School, he didn't have a weapon, Bafagih said, adding he also didn't have a criminal record or a history of bad behaviour. Aside from a fight last year at his high school, he had never before been involved with police. And at around 5-foot-7 and 135 pounds, the baby-faced teen, described by a teacher as a "bright, hardworking B-plus student," was hardly a menacing presence.

Bafagih said her son loved basketball and aspired to be a mechanical engineer. "Why did they kill him? Why didn't they catch him if he made a mistake? They could have grabbed him. Why did they shoot him? It is a shock what they did to him. It is so painful."

The Special Investigations Unit is probing the incident that unfolded just east of the DVP around 9:30 p.m. Wednesday, but officials have released few details. The SIU is a civilian government agency that investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that result in serious injury or death.

Police sources said a couple of officers on routine patrol caught two teens trying to rob another youth before one officer, on the force for five years, shot Al Nadhir following an altercation. Eight other officers are considered witnesses and police seized a replica handgun at the scene.
A friend of Al Nadhir present that night surrendered to police the next day, relatives confirm. He is charged with armed robbery.
Al Nadhir, who had bruises on his face and a bullet wound on the left side of his neck, relatives said, was taken to St. Michael's Hospital where he died before midnight.
Bafagih said she can't understand why no one told her about her son before 6 a.m. the following morning. Police told Al Nadhir's family that the teen wasn't carrying any identification, she said.
"He had his wallet and his cellphone," she said. "All those things we don't know where they are now."

Al Nadhir, who worked part-time as a dishwasher at the Spaghetti Factory restaurant on the Esplanade. and is known to friends as "Al Weezy," got home from school in the late afternoon Wednesday, relatives said. He had picked up McDonald's sandwiches to share with one of his three sisters for dinner.
After running an errand for Bafagih, he went to a friend's house to play video games. He spoke to his mother around 6:30 p.m. by cellphone.
"I told him to come home," she said. "I felt something was going to happen. I told him `I don't like Halloween. I don't like crowds.' He just laughed at me."

When her son didn't make his 10 p.m. curfew, Bafagih began calling his cellphone every few minutes, she said, until it was turned off shortly before 1 a.m. That's when she walked to a police precinct nearby.
"It is not his behaviour to be late," she said. "I was worried." She called police again around 4:30 a.m.

Defence lawyer Joseph Markson, representing the officer who shot Al Nadhir, feels for the family and said his client is "grief stricken" over the incident. But he's confident the facts will show that the "involved officer's use of force was necessary and justified."
A vigil is being planned for tomorrow evening.
